# Amaterasu — the app, running, on your machine

**Nature: Transmuter.** It runs declared machinery and a long-running local process; it writes no
code and sends nothing (a **deploy** is **G3**).

> **Build what I am working on — here, in this checkout or this worktree — start it on the target I
> said, and tell me the exact command so I can run it myself.**

Phase four of `ren`, after [`kokusen`](../kokusen/SKILL.md); it never pushes or opens anything. **Every rule of the declaration it executes is
[`docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md`](../../../docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md) § *Launch declaration rules***.

## 0. Standalone entry

[`docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md`](../../../docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md) (§ 4 for a composite's skip; plugin
root per [PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Authority every phase shares*). Cold it adds **P1**
and **P2**, read with § 3 — **which checkout this is**, core or a worktree, named in the launch line.
**The launch shows the tree on disk, not a commit**: name uncommitted paths.

## 1. Invocation

```
/amaterasu [<target>]        # <target> names a key of nen/contract.json → project.launch
/amaterasu help              # the target guide (§ 1b); launches nothing
```

With no argument the target is `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`. **There is no built-in default
and none is ever guessed** — a wrong build on a wrong device is not undone by relaunching. A
missing argument or configuration item is asked for and set up inline (`missing-argument`,
`missing-configuration`; [`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § 4 *Ask, set up, continue*), a
launch target set up through [`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md).

| What the declaration says | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| `project.launch` **absent** or **empty** | record `no launch target declared; skipped`, naming `nen/contract.json`, and continue |
| `launch.default` **`null`**, no argument, **no** declared targets | the same, naming `launch.default` |
| `launch.default` **`null`** but targets **are** declared, no argument | **the case that asks**: the guide's rows as the options |
| an argument naming an undeclared target | **the trigger to ask**: name it, print the guide, its rows as the options (or one set up through `jujutsu`), **never a near-match** |

**Asking on the no-launch case is the defect**: a question the configuration answered, asked every
`ren` turn, trains the maintainer to dismiss it — no question, stop or bell; continue.

**§ 1a · The profile.** Under `nen/workflow.json` → `profile` `fast`, [`ren`](../ren/SKILL.md) § 2a
skips this phase and the launch line reads `deferred by profile fast; the next standard or thorough
turn, or /amaterasu by name, launches` — nothing built or moved (mukai has no launch step).
Named by the maintainer, it runs under any profile.

**§ 1b · The target guide** — `help`, or the maintainer asking what can be launched. Per declared
target, § 4's `--dry-run` from this checkout (it probes nothing), then one row: **the line to
type** (a key with spaces or non-ASCII bytes quoted, byte-exact), **what it lands on**
(`device.name` and kind — physical, simulator, or this host where no `device` is declared), lane and
verb, **default** / **fallback**, and **status** (the dry run's exit: `0` ready, else its first
refusal line). Blocks equal but for `why`/`$comment` are one row, their keys listed as aliases. Then
the checkout it builds (§ 3), and how to add a target ([`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md)) or move the
default (`launch.default`). No targets: say so, with the canonical block's pointer. **`help` is
reserved** — a target keyed `help` is a defect to rename. After every launch, one line names the
other targets and `/amaterasu help`.

## 2. The parameters, and the completion the launch owes

| Value | File → key |
|---|---|
| The default target and the disconnected-device fallback | `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`, `launch.fallback` |
| The targets — verb, args, device, after-steps, lane, artifact | `nen/contract.json` → `project.launch.<target>` (LAUNCH-MIGRATION) |
| The verb's command line, and where it runs | `project.verbs.<lane>.<verb>`, `project.lanes.<lane>.cwd` |

**`nen shu dev|run --target <name>` executes the whole block** — the probe, the lane's verb with
`args` appended, the after-steps with both substitutions. **With no `nen/workflow.json`**
([PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Invocation and parsing*) there is **no** `launch.default`
and **no** `launch.fallback`: with targets declared, print the guide and ask; with none, § 1's
no-launch case.

**Physical-device completion.** The lane must build for the target's **actual platform** — check the
dry run's lane, destination, artifact substitution and after-steps first. **An iPhone target
wired to a simulator build is an incomplete declaration** (a simulator `.app` named in `after[]` is no
device artifact): repair it within authorized scope or record the blocker through
[the discovery protocol](../../../docs/DISCOVERY.md). **Success is the device build, its install and
the launch, each reported**; a dry run or build-only result is **`launch incomplete`**, and missing
install/launch steps are a declaration gap even at exit `0`. **Record discovery is Nen's shared launch
resolver's** ([nen#204](https://github.com/zheref/nen/issues/204)); a temporary normalizer stays
**linked** with owner and removal condition; **no extraction key is added to an older binary.**

## 3. The session's own checkout — core or the worktree it works in

**A launch builds the tree the session works in**, so a worktree's progress reaches the device
without switching back (the maintainer's ruling, [`docs/ROSTER.md`](../../../docs/ROSTER.md)
§ *Rulings of 2026-09-29*, ruling 4). **`--repo` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the session's
working directory** — never core resolved from a worktree, never another checkout.

- **Name the tree**: the launch line says `core` or `worktree <path>`, the branch, the short HEAD and
  every uncommitted path — the device runs the last tree launched onto it, from whichever checkout.
- **A worktree's local setup is copied from core, never invented.** A `path` precondition failing
  here that core satisfies (a gitignored `local.properties` or `.xcconfig`): copy that file from
  `nen wc worktrees --repo . --json`'s `core`, never over an existing one, never staged, named in the
  launch line. An uninitialised submodule: `git submodule update --init --recursive` here. A file
  core lacks too is the precondition's refusal, relayed.
- **Shared resources**: a declared `port` precondition refuses a port another checkout's app holds;
  an argv writing build output outside the checkout (an absolute derived-data path) is shared by
  every checkout — say so.
- **From core, read `nen wc swap --status --repo <core>`** first: an active swap
  ([`amenotejikara`](../amenotejikara/SKILL.md)) is **named** in the launch line; a status that does
  not answer (exit `1`/`2`) is **refused** — no launch on a half-swapped core.
- **Only the maintainer's session launches**: a subagent, a parallel effort or a temporary clone
  reports § 4's dry-run argv verbatim and stops ([`ren`](../ren/SKILL.md) § 3).

## 4. Resolving the device, the dry run, and the command you paste

**The probe's three outcomes are LAUNCH-MIGRATION's**; what this skill does with each:

| Outcome | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| Present **and usable** | substitute its id into `{device.id}` in the after-steps |
| **Present but NOT usable** | **Refuse; never the simulator fallback** — it is plugged in, one tap from working. With `readyWhen`, **nen already refused at exit `5`** (device, state seen, states accepted): relay it and name the on-device step that closes it ([`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md) § 3). With **no** rule nen reports it resolved: read the probe's state column and **report the missing `readyWhen` as a declaration defect** |
| **Absent** | **Report it by name** — *"`<device.name>` is not connected; the probe saw: `<what it listed>`"* — then fall back to `launch.fallback`, saying so and naming it |
| Absent, `launch.fallback` `null` | say so and stop: plugging one in is an on-device act, picking another a guess |
| No `device` declared | straight to the dry run |

```bash
nen shu <verb> --repo <the session's checkout> --target <name> [--lane <lane>] --dry-run [--json]
nen shu <verb> --repo <the session's checkout> --target <name> [--lane <lane>]
```

- **`<verb>` is `project.launch.<target>.verb`, exactly** — `dev` or `run`, closed; nen carries no
  target across the two (the other is exit `2` naming the fix). With `--target`, **the declared verb
  is checked before the lane's seat**, so an exit `4` there is a **real** seat, quoted as one.
- Dry run and pasted argv: [PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Running a declared verb* —
  **copied, never re-typed**.
- **One bare line whether or not the target declares `args`** (nen appends them); **a `--lane`
  contradicting `project.launch.<name>.lane` is exit `2` naming both**.
- `dev`/`run` are **long-running**: `--json` without `--dry-run` is exit `2`, and **the launch is never
  backgrounded** to free the terminal — say the app is running and what holds it.
- **Exit codes** per `claude/agents/kurapika.md` § *The `shu` verbs*; here `1` is a declared step
  failing — **say which: build, install or launch** — hand authored-code failures to
  [`rasengan`](../rasengan/SKILL.md), a failed install or launch being incomplete delivery; `2` on a
  precondition in a worktree is § 3's copy first; `3` an excluded host, a **G5**, never retried; `4` a
  real seat, quoted, then the repository's documented command run and said; `5` the program not on `PATH`.
- **The after-steps are nen's**, in the same `--target` call, nothing by hand. **Quote the dry run's
  `substitutes:` line**, not `artifacts:` — what the child receives, not what the build produces.

## 5. Residue

**By hand:** § 3's copy of core's local files and submodule init, and § 1b's guide (no nen verb lists
`project.launch`). **Reading device state with no `readyWhen`** is residue **with a fix**, lapsing when
a jujutsu PR writes the rule. **No default target ever**, **no `--` passthrough** (an undeclared argv
is an unreviewed one), and **nothing in nen stops a long-running child**.

## 6. Authority and hard limits

- **Permitted:** run the lane's declared build/`dev` row from the session's checkout, run a declared
  device probe, run the declared `after` steps, copy a gitignored file § 3 names from core, print the
  guide, hand back the exact command.
- **Not permitted:** `nen shu deploy --run` in any form (**G3**, row `release-go`); any push, commit,
  PR, label or release. **Not a gate event**: a disconnected
  device with no declared fallback is a stop-and-say, and an unsupported host (`3`) is its one **G5**.
- **Never launches a checkout other than the session's own**, **never from a subagent or parallel
  effort**, and **never overwrites, stages or invents** a local file § 3 copies.
- **Never falls back to a simulator for a present-but-unusable device**, to an undeclared device, or
  silently; **never invents a target**, and **never asks when the declaration already answered** (§ 1).
- **Never types a `shu` subcommand the target did not declare**, or drops `--target` to get past exit `2`.
- **Never substitutes a plausible command for a declared one**, re-types the pasted command from
  memory, or runs the bare lane verb for a target that declares `args`.
- **Never claims the app is running** on a dry run or unread exit code.
